Subject: MAP kickoff: performance benchmarks & close timeline

Jonas / Redwood team,

Thanks again for yesterday's demo. We want to formalize a MAP so our execs can sign off on procurement by end of May. Primary asks for the MAP: clear performance benchmarks (latency P50/P95, TTFT, tokens/sec), concurrency targets for 50/100 sessions, and a recommendation on GPU family for our expected workload.

Current constraints: 8k token context, mixes of short prompts (20-80 tokens) and long context loads (1–2k tokens), 12 reqs/sec expected steady state with bursts to 75 reqs/sec. Budget sensitivity — total monthly infra target ~$25k.

Can you outline test plan, acceptance criteria, and a proposed test window? Also happy to share sample prompt sets.

—Taylor
Director, AI Platform
AcmeCorp

Hi Taylor — appreciate the context. High level proposal below; Marissa (solutions) and Ben (bench) are looped in to own delivery.

Summary proposal (short):
- Test window: May 4–5 (24–48h runs).
- Targets: P50 < 120ms, P95 < 450ms for short prompts; TTFT (first token) < 250ms for typical chat turns; throughput target 700–1,200 tok/s per GPU depending on model variant.
- Hardware to test: A100 80GB (full), H100 80GB (full), L40S (48GB), plus representative MIG slices (A100 A40 MIG 7g/14g equivalents).
- Acceptance: identify config that meets latency SLOs at 12 rps steady state + 3x burst with cost estimate under $25k/month if possible.

Next steps: please share a canonical prompt set and we will provision runs. We will send a formal MAP doc with milestones by EOD May 3.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber

1) Objectives- Produce a recommendation for production GPU family + MIG sizing- Verify latency (P50/P95), TTFT, and sustained throughput at target concurrency- Provide runbook for scaling and fallback (H100 vs A100 fallbacks)

2) Test matrix (we will run the following):
- Model: acme-chat-2 (quantized fp16 and int8 variants)
- Hardware: H100 (full), A100 (full), L40S (full), A100 MIG slices (1g/2g/7g simulated)- Workloads: mix of short (20–80 tokens) 60% / medium (200–800) 30% / long (1k–2k) 10%- Concurrency profiles: 12 rps constant, 36 rps (2x), 75 rps burst (6x)

3) Metrics and acceptance- Latency P50/P95 (token-level and overall response)- TTFT (first token)- Tokens/sec and effective qps per GPU- Memory headroom and OOM recovery behavior

Acceptance criteria (for GA recommendation):
- P50 short-turn < 120ms AND P95 short-turn < 450ms at 12 rps steady state- TTFT median < 250ms- Sustained throughput meets 12 rps with 30% headroom for bursts- Solution cost projection <= $25k/mo (hosted pricing estimate)

4) Responsibilities- Redwood bench (Ben): execute runs, collect perf artifacts, produce CSV summary and runnotes- Redwood solutions (Marissa): MAP doc, rollout recommendations, canary config- Acme: provide prompt set, dataset for long-context tests, and sign-off window for run dates May 4–5

5) Deliverables and timeline- May 3 EOD: MAP v1 (this email + PDF)- May 4–5: benchmark runs- May 6 EOD: perf summary, recommended fleet (A100/H100/L40S), MIG guidance and cost estimate

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Taylor Nguyen <taylor@acmecorp.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-05T10:00:00-07:00
Subject: ACME perf run results: H100 vs A100 vs L40S + MIG notes

Taylor / Marissa — attached is the raw CSV and runnotes. Below is an executive summary; full CSV attached (perf_summary_h100_vs_a100_vs_l40s.csv) and mig_vs_fullgpu-runnotes.txt.

Executive summary (24h steady-state + burst tests):
- Setup: acme-chat-2 fp16 model, sequence dist matching ACME prompt set, synthetic clients for concurrency. All runs measured token-level latencies and end-to-end response times.

Key numbers (median values across short-turn workload):
- H100 (full): P50 token = 78ms, P95 token = 330ms, TTFT median = 140ms, sustained tokens/s per GPU = 1,050 tok/s. Handled 75 rps bursts with 15% latency uplift (P95 ~380ms).
- A100 (full): P50 token = 110ms, P95 token = 480ms, TTFT median = 210ms, sustained tokens/s per GPU = 820 tok/s. Burst P95 ~620ms and occasional queueing beyond 90 rps without autoscale.
- L40S (full): P50 token = 95ms, P95 token = 410ms, TTFT median = 185ms, sustained tokens/s per GPU = 920 tok/s. More cost-efficient per-hour on targeted clouds but memory constrained for 2k-context long-context experiments.
- A100 MIG (7g equivalent): P50 token = 160ms, P95 token = 720ms, TTFT median = 320ms, sustained tokens/s per MIG-slice = ~430 tok/s. Good for consolidation but significant P95 penalty; multi-tenant mixes increased tail latencies unpredictably in our tests.

Notes and recommendations:
1) If lowest latency P95 is top priority: H100 recommended. It met P95 < 450ms for short-turns and had best TTFT.
2) If cost-constrained to ~ $25k/mo: a mixed fleet (L40S primary + H100 for critical low-latency endpoints) hits a balance; L40S handles most steady-state cheaply, H100 used for high-priority routes and burst capacity.
3) MIG: useful for dev/staging and constrained budgets, but for production-critical customer-facing routes we saw unacceptable P95 variability. Consider 1–2x MIG hosts for non-critical workloads only.
4) Long-context (1–2k): only H100 and A100 full GPUs reliably handled batch sizes without spilling; L40S required prompt truncation or smaller batch sizes.

Deliverables attached: perf_summary_h100_vs_a100_vs_l40s.csv, mig_vs_fullgpu-runnotes.txt. I can produce a consolidated cost projection (hosted vs dedicated) by EOD May 6.

—Ben Carter
Benchmarking Engineer, Redwood Inference

2) Cost snapshot: Hosted estimate $22k/mo (for the tested traffic profile, includes autoscale buffer). Dedicated reserved baseline estimate $19k/mo with a 12-month commit (detailed numbers in Drive link).
